extracted.intended_audience: advanced_undergraduate or beginning_graduate students in algebraic topology; readers learning fundamental group, covering spaces, and K(G,1) constructions
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and constructions relating graphs, trees, covering spaces, and K(G,1) spaces; includes proofs that free-group phenomena correspond to graph topologies and a procedure (graphs of groups) to assemble K(G,1) spaces for larger groups from smaller ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1A.2 – π1 of a connected graph is free
rubrics_metrics.description: For a connected graph X with maximal tree T, π1(X) is a free group with basis the classes [fα] corresponding to the edges eα of X − T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct loops fα by going from basepoint x0 along paths in T to an endpoint of eα, across eα, and back along T. The quotient X/T is a wedge of circles; the images of these loops give a basis. Consequence: adjoining any edge to a maximal tree produces nontrivial π1; a graph is a tree iff it is simply-connected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1A.3 – Coverings of graphs are graphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Every covering space of a graph is a graph, with vertices and edges the lifts of the vertices and edges in the base graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a covering p: X˜→X, the preimage of the 0-skeleton gives vertices and path-lifting gives lifts of each edge-interval Iα defining edges in the cover. The lifted topology matches the original since the covering projection is a local homeomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1A.4 – Subgroups of free groups are free
rubrics_metrics.description: Every subgroup of a free group is free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent the free group F as π1 of a wedge of circles X. For any subgroup G ⊂ F use covering space theory (there is a covering p: X˜→X with p∗(π1(X˜)) = G) and Lemma 1A.3 to see X˜ is a graph; then Proposition 1A.2 shows π1(X˜) ≈ G is free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal trees and uniqueness of nonbacktracking edgepaths
rubrics_metrics.description: In a tree X with chosen base vertex v0, there is a unique nonbacktracking edgepath joining any two points; vertices can be given a height so each vertex has exactly one downward edge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct maximal tree Y by levels Yn. Height function monotone on edges; unique downward edgepath gives unique nonbacktracking representative in each homotopy class. Equivalently, a connected graph is a tree iff it contains no circle subgraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of K(G,1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A path-connected space whose fundamental group is isomorphic to a given group G and which has a contractible universal covering space is called a K(G,1) space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The '1' refers to π1. K(G,1) spaces have contractible universal covers, so their homotopy type depends only on G; they are Eilenberg–MacLane spaces for n=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of K(G,1) spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete examples and families of K(G,1)s: S1 for G=Z; connected graphs for free groups; closed surfaces with infinite π1 (all except S2 and RP2); RP∞ for Z2; infinite-dimensional lens spaces S∞/Zm for Zm; products K(G,1)×K(H,1)=K(G×H,1); complements of certain subspaces in S3 (e.g., knot complements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each example includes reasoning: e.g., universal cover of a graph is a tree (contractible); RP∞ universal cover is S∞ which is contractible via explicit homotopies; product of universal covers is contractible, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of EG and BG (bar construction) producing K(G,1)
rubrics_metrics.description: EG is a contractible simplicial complex built from ordered tuples [g0,...,gn] with a free G-action by left multiplication; BG = EG/G is a K(G,1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe simplices as [g0,g0g1,...,g0g1...gn] and use bar notation [g1|...|gn] for simplices of BG. EG deformation via sliding toward [e]; action is free so quotient is a CW complex with one vertex; BG is often infinite-dimensional but functorial in G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1B.8 – Homotopy type of K(G,1) determined by G
rubrics_metrics.description: The homotopy type of a CW complex K(G,1) is uniquely determined by the group G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from Proposition 1B.9: any isomorphism of fundamental groups is induced by maps between K(G,1)'s that are inverse up to homotopy, hence K(G,1)'s with isomorphic π1 are homotopy equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1B.9 – Realizing homomorphisms by maps into K(G,1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be a connected CW complex and Y a K(G,1). Every homomorphism π1(X,x0)→π1(Y,y0) is induced by a map (X,x0)→(Y,y0) that is unique up to homotopy fixing the basepoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct map on 0- and 1-skeletons to realize images of 1-cells, extend over 2-cells because attaching maps become nullhomotopic under the chosen homomorphism, and higher cells extend because lifts to the contractible universal cover are nullhomotopic. For multiple 0-cells use a maximal tree to collapse to the basepoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / construction of a graph of groups and its K-space K(Γ)
rubrics_metrics.description: A graph of groups: an oriented connected graph Γ with a group Gv at each vertex and edge homomorphisms ϕe from tail group to head group; build a space by placing K(Gv,1) at each vertex and attaching mapping cylinders for the edge maps to form a CW complex KΓ whose π1 is the 'fundamental group of the graph of groups' (graph product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One may take BGv or any K(Gv,1) at vertices and fill mapping cylinders along edges; the cell-structure can be subdivided canonically if desired. Van Kampen computes π1 as a group obtained by amalgamating according to the edge homomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1B.11 – Injective edge maps give K(G,1) and injective inclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: If all the edge homomorphisms ϕe are injective in a graph of groups, then the assembled space KΓ is a K(G,1) and the inclusions K(Gv,1) ↪ KΓ induce injective maps on π1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the universal cover by gluing universal covers of mapping cylinders in a treelike inductive fashion to produce a contractible cover K̃; projection K̃→KΓ is a covering so KΓ is K(G,1). A nullhomotopy of a loop in some vertex K(Gv,1) lifts to a nullhomotopy in the vertex universal cover, so inclusion is π1-injective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special cases: free products with amalgamation and HNN extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Free product with amalgamation A *C B arises from graph of groups A ← C → B with injective maps; HNN extensions arise from a graph of groups with one vertex and one edge where two monomorphisms from C to A specify relations tϕ(c)t−1 = ψ(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Van Kampen's theorem gives the algebraic description. Examples include realizing knot complements and torus-knot complements as such constructions; certain semidirect products and Klein bottle groups arise as HNN-type constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and properties of the universal cover of KΓ
rubrics_metrics.description: The universal cover K̃ is constructed as a union of universal covers of the mapping cylinders glued together in an inductive treelike pattern, producing a contractible space whose orbit space under deck transformations recovers the original graph Γ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a universal cover of one mapping cylinder and attach copies of universal covers of neighboring mapping cylinders at boundary components, repeating inductively to form K̃ = ⋃ Kn. Deformation retractions of successive stages show K̃ is contractible. The arrangement reflects an action of π1(KΓ) on a tree whose quotient is Γ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treelike arrangement and action on Bass–Serre tree
rubrics_metrics.description: The mapping cylinders in the universal cover assemble in a treelike pattern; there is a tree T with a vertex for each copy of a universal cover of K(Gv,1) and edges where mapping cylinders connect them. π1(KΓ) acts on T with orbit space Γ, and graphs of groups correspond to groups acting on trees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets up the Bass–Serre correspondence: graph-of-groups data ↔ group actions on trees. One may restrict definitions to oriented subdivided graphs to match standard Bass–Serre conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications and consequences listed in exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercises collect consequences and applications: Euler characteristic and rank relations (rank π1 = 1−χ for finite graphs), residual finiteness of free groups via finite-index normal subgroups, finite number of subgroups of given index for finitely generated groups, existence of finite graphs extending finite subgraphs in covers, Baumslag–Solitar group presentations from certain graphs of groups, and finiteness properties of graph products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises suggest methods: use covering space arguments, liftings, finite-sheeted coverings, and van Kampen to deduce group-theoretic properties from topological constructions. Several exercises direct explicit constructions (e.g., universal cover as T×R in some cases).
